# Dock

A floating rail of icon controls that morphs, in place, into a labelled menu with drill-down layers. One box animates its own width, height and corner, so the rail becomes the menu instead of opening a second surface.

```tsx
<Dock aria-label="Koala workspace" trigger="hover">
  <DockItem icon={<SquaresFour weight="bold" />} label="Components" shortcut="⌘1" active />
  <DockItem icon={<Browsers weight="bold" />} label="Templates" shortcut="⌘2" />
  <DockItem icon={<Flask weight="bold" />} label="Playground" shortcut="⌘3" />

  <DockGroup icon={<Palette weight="bold" />} label="Appearance">
    <DockLabel>Theme</DockLabel>
    <DockItem icon={<Sun weight="bold" />} label="Light" active />
    <DockItem icon={<Coffee weight="bold" />} label="Cream" />
    <DockItem icon={<Moon weight="bold" />} label="Dark" />
    <DockItem icon={<MoonStars weight="bold" />} label="Moonlight" />
  </DockGroup>

  <DockGroup icon={<Buildings weight="bold" />} label="Workspace">
    <DockItem icon={<UsersThree weight="bold" />} label="Members" />
    <DockItem icon={<ChartLine weight="bold" />} label="Usage" />
    <DockItem icon={<CreditCard weight="bold" />} label="Billing" />
    <DockSeparator />
    <DockItem icon={<Key weight="bold" />} label="API keys" />
  </DockGroup>

  <DockExpander />
</Dock>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add dock
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/dock/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import {
  Dock,
  DockItem,
  DockGroup,
  DockLabel,
  DockSeparator,
  DockExpander,
} from "@/components/ui/dock"

<Dock aria-label="Workspace">
  <DockItem icon={<SquaresFour weight="bold" />} label="Components" shortcut="⌘1" active />
  <DockGroup icon={<Palette weight="bold" />} label="Appearance">
    <DockLabel>Theme</DockLabel>
    <DockItem icon={<Sun weight="bold" />} label="Light" />
  </DockGroup>
  <DockExpander />
</Dock>
```

The label is a prop, not children, because the dock renders it twice: as the tooltip on the collapsed icon, and as the row's text in the panel. One source, two shapes.

## Variants

Floating is the default: the house's elevated popover surface, because a dock is chrome and chrome should inherit the page's theme rather than punch a slab of the opposite colour through it. Solid is the inverted slab, for a dock that has to hold its own over a photograph, a canvas or a video. It flips foreground and background rather than hardcoding black, so it reads dark on the light themes and light on the dark ones.

```tsx
{/* floating (default) */}
<Dock aria-label="Floating rail">…</Dock>

{/* solid */}
<Dock aria-label="Solid rail" variant="solid">…</Dock>

{/* both shapes: pass `expanded` to hold the panel open */}
<Dock aria-label="Floating panel" expanded>…</Dock>
<Dock aria-label="Solid panel" variant="solid" expanded>…</Dock>
```

## Sizes

`size` is the dock's own density axis, not the page's comfortable/compact knob: a floating control bar that shrinks to form-compact becomes hard to hit. Every step is built on one identity, 8px padding + half the icon button = the rail's corner, so the buttons come out as true circles and concentric inside the pill at all three sizes.

```tsx
<Dock size="sm">…</Dock>
<Dock size="md">…</Dock>  {/* default */}
<Dock size="lg">…</Dock>
```

## Layers

A `DockGroup` is a drill-down. Opening it replaces the panel's contents with a “Back” row and its children, and the box resizes to fit: no second surface, no popup beside a popup. Groups nest, so a group inside a group is one layer deeper. Press `Esc` to step back one layer at a time.

```tsx
<Dock aria-label="Canvas" variant="solid" defaultExpanded closeOnSelect={false}>
  <DockItem icon={<Selection weight="bold" />} label="Select" shortcut="V" active />
  <DockItem icon={<FrameCorners weight="bold" />} label="Frame" shortcut="F" />
  <DockItem icon={<TextT weight="bold" />} label="Text" shortcut="T" />

  <DockGroup icon={<Export weight="bold" />} label="Export">
    <DockLabel>Format</DockLabel>
    <DockItem icon={<FilePng weight="bold" />} label="PNG" active />
    <DockItem icon={<FileSvg weight="bold" />} label="SVG" />
    <DockItem icon={<FilePdf weight="bold" />} label="PDF" />
    <DockSeparator />

    {/* a group inside a group: one layer deeper */}
    <DockGroup icon={<ArrowsOutSimple weight="bold" />} label="Scale">
      <DockItem icon={<Ruler weight="bold" />} label="1x" active />
      <DockItem icon={<Ruler weight="bold" />} label="2x" />
      <DockItem icon={<Ruler weight="bold" />} label="3x" />
    </DockGroup>
  </DockGroup>
</Dock>
```

## Captions and shortcuts

`DockLabel` sorts a long panel into topics, and `shortcut` puts a muted keycap at the end of a row. Both live in the panel only: the rail has no room for a word, so while the dock is collapsed the shortcut rides in the tooltip beside the label instead, as a real cap.

```tsx
<Dock aria-label="Editor menu" expanded>
  <DockLabel>Insert</DockLabel>
  <DockItem icon={<FrameCorners weight="bold" />} label="Frame" shortcut="F" />
  <DockItem icon={<TextT weight="bold" />} label="Text" shortcut="T" />
  <DockItem icon={<Shapes weight="bold" />} label="Shape" shortcut="R" />
  <DockSeparator />
  <DockLabel>Canvas</DockLabel>
  <DockItem icon={<Ruler weight="bold" />} label="Rulers" shortcut="⇧R" active />
  <DockItem icon={<SquaresFour weight="bold" />} label="Grid" shortcut="⌘G" />
</Dock>
```

## Trigger

`trigger="click"` is the default and the right pick on touch. `trigger="hover"` expands when the pointer lands on the expander and collapses shortly after it leaves the dock. The grace period is there so crossing a 2px gap on the way to a row never dismisses the thing you are reaching for.

```tsx
<Dock aria-label="Opens on click">…</Dock>

<Dock aria-label="Opens on hover" trigger="hover">…</Dock>
```

## States

`active` marks the current destination: a chip, a heavier label and a brand-coloured glyph, the same answer the Sidebar gives its active item (it also sets `aria-current="page"`). `disabled` takes a control out of the roving focus, and `DockSeparator` is axis-aware: a vertical tick in the rail, a horizontal rule in the panel.

```tsx
<Dock aria-label="States">
  <DockItem icon={<Gauge weight="bold" />} label="Overview" shortcut="⌘1" active />
  <DockItem icon={<ChartLine weight="bold" />} label="Traffic" shortcut="⌘2" />
  <DockItem icon={<Lightning weight="bold" />} label="Realtime (Pro)" disabled />
  <DockSeparator />
  <DockItem icon={<Export weight="bold" />} label="Export report" />
  <DockExpander />
</Dock>
```

## Links

Pass `asChild` with your own element and the dock renders its icon and label inside it, so a nav dock can use `next/link` and keep client-side routing.

```tsx
<Dock aria-label="Documentation" expanded>
  <DockItem icon={<SquaresFour weight="bold" />} label="Components" asChild active>
    <Link href="/docs/components/dock" />
  </DockItem>
  <DockItem icon={<Swatches weight="bold" />} label="Colors" asChild>
    <Link href="/docs/foundations/colors" />
  </DockItem>
</Dock>
```

## Controlled

Drive the shape yourself with `expanded` / `onExpandedChange`, to open the dock from a keyboard shortcut, or to keep it open while a tour points at it.

```tsx
const [expanded, setExpanded] = React.useState(false)

<Dock
  aria-label="Controlled dock"
  expanded={expanded}
  onExpandedChange={setExpanded}
>
  …
  <DockExpander />
</Dock>
```

## API reference

### Dock

The morphing box and the roving-focus root (Radix `Toolbar.Root`, so it forwards `dir`, `loop` and the rest). Takes `variant` (floating · solid), `size` (sm · md · lg), `expanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange`, `trigger` (click · hover), `closeOnSelect`, `tooltipPlacement`, and `static` to drop the press-scale across every control. The arrow-key axis follows the shape: horizontal in the rail, vertical in the panel.

### DockItem

A destination or an action. Takes `icon`, `label` (required), `shortcut`, `active`, `disabled`, `onSelect`, and `asChild` to hand the control to a link. Collapsed it is an icon with the label as its tooltip; expanded it is a labelled row.

### DockGroup

A drill-down layer. Takes `icon`, `label`, `value` (its identity in the open path, defaulting to the label), `backLabel` (default `"Back"`) and `disabled`. Its children are the rows of its layer; pressing it from the rail expands the dock straight into that branch.

### DockLabel · DockExpander · DockSeparator

`DockLabel` is a caption over a run of rows (panel only). `DockExpander` is the control that turns the rail into the panel (`label`, or your own `children` in place of the menu glyph); it exists only in the rail, because once the labels are on screen there is nothing left for it to reveal. `DockSeparator` is the axis-aware hairline (Radix `Toolbar.Separator`).

## FAQ

### How is this different from Toolbar?

Toolbar is a band of controls: it stays one shape and groups icon buttons, toggles and dropdown triggers. Dock is a navigation surface that changes shape: it collapses to a rail of icons and expands, in place, into a labelled menu with drill-down layers. Both are built on Radix Toolbar, so they share the roving focus and arrow-key model; reach for Toolbar to act on something (a format bar, a tool rail) and for Dock to go somewhere.

### Why does the box animate instead of opening a menu next to it?

Because the rail and the menu are the same object. The root measures its own content with a ResizeObserver and writes the next width/height, then CSS tweens between them behind overflow-hidden, so the incoming layer is revealed by a box that is still growing. A popup beside the rail would be a second surface to track; this is one.

### Why is the label a prop instead of children?

Because the dock renders it twice. Collapsed, the label is the tooltip on the icon (and the button's aria-label); expanded, it is the row's text. Passing it once as a prop keeps those two in sync and is what lets the same declarative tree describe both shapes.

### When should I use solid instead of floating?

When the dock sits over something that is not your page: a photograph, a video, a map, a design canvas. Floating inherits the page's popover surface and is the right default everywhere else. Solid flips foreground and background rather than hardcoding black, so it stays legible in all four themes instead of becoming a dark hole on a dark page.

### How deep can groups nest?

As deep as you like. A DockGroup opens a layer, and a group inside it opens the next one; the Back row always returns to the parent. Only the layer on screen is mounted, so a branch you have not opened costs nothing.

### How do I close it?

Click outside, press Escape (which steps back one layer at a time before it closes), or choose an item, and closeOnSelect is on by default. With trigger="hover" it also collapses shortly after the pointer leaves, on a short grace period so a 2px gap on the way to a row never dismisses it.

### Is it keyboard accessible?

Yes. It is a Radix Toolbar: the whole dock is a single Tab stop and arrow keys move between controls, on the axis that matches the current shape. Opening a layer moves focus to its first row, but only when you drove the change, so a hover-driven expand never yanks focus away from what you were doing.

### Does it follow the page's comfortable/compact density?

No, by design, the same call as Toolbar. Its size axis (sm / md / lg) is the dock's own density knob, because a floating control bar that shrinks to form-compact becomes hard to hit. Set size explicitly, or pass it from useDensity() yourself if you do want it to track.

### Does it respect reduced motion?

Yes. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the box resizes instantly instead of tweening, the layer swap does not animate, and the tactile press-scale is dropped, and every functional state (hover, active chip, focus ring) stays exactly as it is.

### Where should I put it on the page?

Position it yourself, the way you would any floating surface: typically fixed, bottom-centered. The dock grows from its own top-left corner, so anchoring it by bottom makes the panel open upward, which is what you want above a page's content.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add dock` writes `components/ui/dock/`. Import from `@/components/ui/dock`:

- Components and helpers: `Dock`, `DockItem`, `DockGroup`, `DockLabel`, `DockExpander`, `DockSeparator`, `dockVariants`
- Types: `DockProps`, `DockItemProps`, `DockGroupProps`, `DockLabelProps`, `DockExpanderProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `kbd`, `tooltip`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `hit-area`, `motion`, `tv`, `utils`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`, `radix-ui`
